headline_marked: [[Google's simulated fruit fly brain 'mines Bitcoin']] in web browser proof of concept
headline: Google's simulated fruit fly brain 'mines Bitcoin' in web browser proof of concept
summary: FutureBit's HashFly project uses a simulated fruit fly connectome to mine Bitcoin as a proof of concept. The company suggests real organic neurons could offer 10x the efficiency of 3nm ASICs.
details: FutureBit, known for its Apollo series of ASIC miners, has launched HashFly, a proof of concept for an "organic neuron Bitcoin miner based on the fly brain." It leverages Google's recently shared fruit fly connectome. The company claims that if scaled on real organic neurons, it could achieve ~1 watt per terahash, which is 10x the efficiency of the best silicon 3nm ASICs.

The HashFly website allows users to participate in this experiment. By clicking 'Mine', a web app simulates "2,914 traces firing" within the fly's brain. This represents a small subset of the full 165,122 reconstructed neurons in the MaleCNS v1.0 fruit fly connectome.

The simulation focuses on the fly's simulated photoreceptors, which read a block header. Specific PPL101 cells then light up when a double-SHA-256 target is computed. Users can adjust the difficulty, though even at maximum difficulty, it is significantly easier than finding a real Bitcoin hash.

The purpose of this proof of concept is to gain insight into the potential efficiency of organic computing, or wetware. FutureBit's efficiency estimates are based on the total power used by a fruit fly, assuming all neurons could be used for Bitcoin hashing functions and continuously firing.

FutureBit plans to scale up the HashFly demo to simulate all neurons in the dataset with the SHA256 hash function and publish their findings. Current web performance is around 100 kH/s, a stark contrast to the firm's Apollo III ASIC, which delivers up to 18 TH/s.

This project follows other creative uses of Google's fruit fly connectome, which was published recently. Other social media projects have explored using the digitized fly brain to play Doom or engage in financial day trading.

A rival cryptomining scheme, dubbed FlyMiner, also exists, putting a fruit fly connectome under the control of an ASIC miner. However, FlyMiner admits it has "almost zero chance" of actual mining success.

headline_marked: [[Academics host workshop to stop sex]] in self-driving cars, citing reputational risk
headline: Academics host workshop to stop sex in self-driving cars, citing reputational risk
summary: Researchers are holding an industry workshop to brainstorm design interventions that prevent passengers from engaging in antisocial behavior, including sex, in self-driving vehicles, aiming to protect the technology's public image.
details: Researchers led by Pavlo Bazilinskyy from Eindhoven University of Technology are exploring a unique challenge for autonomous vehicles: preventing antisocial behavior, including sex, in robotaxis. Bazilinskyy even researched public transport incidents on PornHub, finding 297 relevant hits.

This week, Bazilinskyy and colleagues are hosting an industry workshop in Gothenburg, Sweden. The event brings together experts to brainstorm physical and design interventions to discourage consensual interactions and other behaviors in self-driving cars.

The academics emphasize that their goal is not to be 'no fun,' but to ensure automated mobility solutions are accepted and trusted by the public. They fear a negative reputation could hinder the technology's significant benefits for the elderly, children, and people with disabilities.

Potential interventions discussed include transparent vehicle designs or blinking lights that activate upon detecting disapproved behavior. The workshop's findings will be used to publish a paper, with broader implications for designing safe communal spaces in future public transit.
